notes: Layout: core/<system>/e<major> is one workspace per dependency system and Bazel major, all on the toy ruleset of toy.bzl (no external ruleset). core/payloads/{upstream,patched} holds the package files the fixture server serves; core/bzlmod/<era>/locks holds the lock `bazel mod deps` made against https://bcr.bazel.build/.

A cell is one run of every bazel_core_ test under one Bazel on one OS, with SOCKET_PATCH_BAZEL_E2E_GROUP=core and no SOCKET_PATCH_BAZEL_E2E_SYSTEM: each test opens the fixture of its own dependency system and reports SKIP (n/a) where the line has none.

network none: the registry files and the one module archive a build fetches are committed (fixtures/bazel/registry), so the cell contacts no host. network archives: Bazel 8.8.2 fetches 12.4 MB of module archives from github.com into the repository cache, and its reports say direct_network; restore that cache (SOCKET_PATCH_BAZEL_E2E_CACHE_ROOT) to keep the fetch to one.

tests lists the Bazel versions each test reports status `ran` on; elsewhere it reports `skipped`. bazel_core_zero_network is claimed where the archives are committed, bazel_core_toy_facts_go_stale from Bazel 8.6.

Every cell ran on macOS arm64 only (2026-11-12). The Linux and Windows cells are unverified: on Windows the registry is served by the fixture server instead of read through --registry=file://, and proof tier 2 is not run.

The committed locks were recorded on macOS arm64; bazel_core_zero_network builds on them in error mode. The same Bazel command (the committed lock in error mode, --registry=file://, --distdir, no network interface) also passed in a Linux arm64 container on 7.7.2 and 9.3.2, outside the test harness. Linux x86_64 has not run.
